passage: Sunday. Pradeep Dada told Siddharth about his own elder brother, a soldier who held a mountain post through a snowstorm. Siddharth forgot to blink. "Weren't you scared for him?" "Every day." Wednesday. Siddharth had broken the classroom window with a ball, and the others had run off. His stomach knotted, but he thought of the soldier and walked to the teacher's table to say it was him. Saturday. He joined Dada at the colony clean-up, dragging a sack of leaves. "Soldiers keep the border," he said. "Somebody has to keep the colony."

qa.a: He broke the classroom window with a ball.

qa.q: What was Siddharth feeling while Dada told the soldier's story?
qa.a: Awe: he forgot to blink and asked whether Dada was scared for his brother.

qa.q: How did Siddharth turn his admiration into action?
qa.a: He told the teacher the truth about the window and joined the colony clean-up.

qa.q: How might Pradeep Dada feel seeing Siddharth at the clean-up?
qa.a: Probably proud and moved, since the story about his brother seems to have reached his grandson.

grounding: Illustrates a child awed by a soldier's story who expresses admiration through honesty and helping the community.
